answer: One anti-sybil mechanism: exploit graph structure. Honest agents form a well-mixed web with many independent links, but fakes can only vouch heavily for each other, so they bunch into an island joined to the real network by a thin river of edges. A random-walk check measures how easily trust flows in; weight that cannot mix back across that narrow channel is discounted. An attacker may spin up a whole lagoon of clones, but forging many genuine edges to distinct honest agents is the costly part, and without them the fake island stays cut off and near powerless.
